records.name: Freelance graphic designer (contests and 1-to-1 projects)
records.summary: Apply to join 99designs as a designer, then compete in client design contests or take paid 1-to-1 projects such as logos and branding.

appeal: Free to sign up, and clients come to the platform, so you do less self-marketing than going solo
Platform fees fall as you move up levels: 15% at Entry, 10% at Mid and 5% at Top on 1-to-1 projects
A way to build a portfolio and client relationships that can continue as 1-to-1 work
watchOuts: Contests are speculative: losing entries aren't paid, and a study of about 38,000 contests found a large share of designers never win a single contest
One paid winner can face hundreds of other entries (TechCrunch)
Acceptance is competitive. A curation team reviews applications, and after two declined attempts you are declined permanently
Entry-level designers can only enter the lower-priced Bronze and Silver contest packages (third-party summary)
Fees: a 15–5% platform fee depending on level, plus a $100 introduction fee for each new client, spread over that client's first $500
Payouts go only through Hyperwallet since January 2026
A March 2026 Trustpilot reviewer said most of the entries they received were AI-generated (anecdotal). 99designs says it has systems to catch rule-breaking designs
Job Bank rates the 2025–2027 outlook for graphic designers and illustrators as Very limited in Ontario, so competition for design work is high
No source names Canada as an eligible designer country. Eligibility is inferred from the platform's worldwide designer base

training.notes: No platform training found. Professional design-software skills and a strong portfolio are expected.

compensation.notes: No official designer earnings figures found. Third-party sites list client logo-contest prices from US$249 (Bronze) to US$1,050 (Platinum); one critical review estimates the winner receives roughly 60% of the contest fee (unverified). 1-to-1 project prices are set by the designer.

reliability.notes: Contest income depends on winning against many entrants. Academic study of about 38,000 contests: a few designers win consistently and many never win.

records.fees: Platform fee on 1-to-1 projects: 15% (Entry), 10% (Mid) or 5% (Top level). A $100 introduction fee per new client, spread over that client's first $500 in charges. Free to sign up.

If accepted at Entry level, enter Bronze or Silver contests or offer 1-to-1 projects, and request a level review after 6 months of activity

records.notFitIf: You're new to design, need dependable income, or object to doing unpaid speculative work.

records.name: Stock photo, video & illustration contributor
records.summary: Sell licences to your photos, videos, vectors and illustrations through Adobe Stock and earn a share of each sale.
records.whatYouDo: You create and upload images, footage or vector art with titles and keywords through the Adobe Stock Contributor portal. Submissions are moderated, and accepted files earn a royalty whenever an Adobe Stock customer licenses them.
appeal: Free to join with an Adobe ID. Adobe says there are no upfront or subscription fees
Adobe's published royalty rate is 33% for photos, vectors and illustrations and 35% for video
Adobe sets per-download royalty floors for large-subscription sales (about $0.33–$0.38, rising with lifetime licences)
Payouts through PayPal, Payoneer or Skrill
watchOuts: Per-download earnings are often under $1. Adobe's own example is about US$0.99 per photo on a 10-licence monthly plan, and as low as $0.33–$0.40 on large plans
You can only request a payout once you have at least US$25 and 45 days have passed since your first sale

Contributors on Adobe's forum report sharp download drops in 2025–2026 (one went from 50–60 to 10–20 a week with 6,200+ assets). Community experts blame competition from AI-generated content, now about half the library (anecdotal)
Forum posters also complain of vague rejections and some account deactivations. Adobe staff don't answer individual account issues on the forum
Without a valid US tax form, Adobe withholds tax at the maximum rate (30%)
Your country of residence is fixed when you create the Adobe ID
You must be 18 or older

training.notes: No required training; must follow Adobe's account, content submission and model-release guidelines.

compensation.notes: Official: royalty 33% (photos, vectors, illustrations) and 35% (video) of the net licence price, based on the US purchase price. Adobe's contributor page shows about $3.30 per download on a small monthly plan, down to $0.33–$0.40 on the largest plans; extended and HD/4K licences pay more. Free-collection placements pay a one-time credit instead. Payout minimum US$25. No typical monthly income is published.

reliability.notes: Income depends on buyer downloads. Adobe community forum threads (2025–2026, anecdotal) report large, unexplained drops in downloads and blame a growing share of AI content.

Accept the Contributor Agreement and read the submission and model-release guidelines
Upload files with titles and keywords and wait for moderation
Link PayPal, Payoneer or Skrill and file a US tax form (non-US residents use a W-8 form) before requesting payment
records.fitsIf: You already create photos, video or vector art and want to earn a little from a growing back catalogue over time.
records.notFitIf: You need predictable income soon or don't want your earnings to depend on an algorithm and a crowded library.

Reviews and a track record can lead to repeat clients

appeal: Canada is one of UserTesting's seven standard contributor countries
Pay for each test is shown up front in your feed
Tests are short: third-party reviews commonly cite about $10 for a roughly 20-minute unmoderated test
The practice test can be done in English or French (or German)

Verify your email and connect a PayPal account in good standing
Complete your profile
Record the practice test in English, French or German
Take screeners in your dashboard and complete the tests you qualify for

Podcast producer jobs found asked for a lot of experience (one Scotiabank posting required 5+ years of podcast, broadcast or similar production)
You need a capable computer and editing software. Their cost was not researched
Freelance demand is irregular, with no guaranteed volume
